overview.description: Hola (meaning 'Nakedness' or 'Naked') is a unique Slavic trick-taking game popular among Ukrainian-Canadians and in parts of Eastern Europe. It stands out from standard Whist-like games because a trick can only be won by playing a card of the SAME rank as the lead, or by playing a wild card (7s and 2s). It shares ancestors with the Czech game Sedma.

timeline: 19th Century: Ancestor games like Sedma popular in the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
Early 20th Century: Carried to Canada by Slavic immigrants.
Present: A hallmark of Ukrainian-Canadian cultural heritage.
history.evolution: While European relatives often use a 32-card deck, the Canadian 'Hola' version typically uses a full 52-card deck.
history.cultural: The name refers to a 'burn' or 'naked' state where a team loses all points if they fail to win a single trick.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (opponents sit opposite).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: 7s and 2s are WILD.
setup.dealing: Deal 4 cards to each player. The remaining cards form a stockpile (Draw Pile). Each player refills their hand to 4 cards after every trick until the deck is gone.

rules.objective: Score points by capturing Aces and Tens (the 'counting cards'). There are 90 total points available (8 counting cards + 10 for the last trick).
rules.gameplay:
1. The lead player plays a card.
2. In turn, others play ANY card. You do not have to follow suit.
3. **Winning the Trick**: To beat the lead, you must play a card of the SAME RANK as the lead, or a WILD card (7 or 2).
4. **Countering**: The lead player can respond by playing another card of the same rank or another wild card to 'take back' the trick. This continues until everyone has passed or played on the lead.
5. The last player to match the lead rank (or play a wild) wins all cards in the trick.

Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: - Aces: 10 points each.
Winning condition: Score points by capturing Aces and Tens (the 'counting cards').

strategy.basic: Keep your wild cards (7s and 2s) for when an opponent leads an Ace or Ten. Don't waste them on low-value tricks.
strategy.intermediate: If you have multiples of a rank (e.g., three 8s), lead one. If someone tries to take it with a wild, you have two more 8s to win it back.
strategy.advanced: Track the wild cards. Knowing how many 2s and 7s are left determines how safe it is to lead a Ten to capture an opponent's Ace.
tips: The 'Last Trick' is vital for the 10-point bonus and can often decide the game.
If you are far behind, try for a 'Hola' to wipe your opponents' score.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck with four suits and thirteen ranks; no jokers. Used for Hola, a Slavic trick-taking game where only cards of matching rank or certain wild cards (7s, 2s) win tricks.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each contain thirteen cards. In Hola, suit matters for following; only the led rank or designated wild cards determine the trick winner.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks Ace through 2 in each suit. In Hola, 7s and 2s act as wild or counter cards; Aces and Tens are high-value captures; other ranks match by identity to win the trick.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Slavic partnership trick-taking game where only matching rank or wild cards win tricks, with a unique countering mechanic.

prompts.human: Welcome to Hola, the Ukrainian-Canadian classic. Play as partnerships in a unique trick-taking game. The lead plays a card. To win, play a card of the SAME RANK or use a wild (7 or 2). Your partner can counter an opponent's play to win the trick back. Capture Aces and Tens for points. Score all 90 points in a hand = Hola = bonus!
prompts.ai: Game: Hola (Ukrainian/Slavic partnership trick-taking). 4 players, 2 partnerships. Setup: 52-card deck, 4 cards per player, stockpile refills. Gameplay: Lead plays card. Others play any card. Win by matching lead rank OR playing 7/2 (wild). Countering allowed. Scoring: Aces (10) + Tens (10) + last trick (10) = 90 total. Hola (all 90) = 170 bonus. First partnership to target wins.

scoring.description: Partnerships score points for taking Aces and Tens (10 points each). Last trick = 10 points. Total 90 points available.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to agreed target (typically 200+ points) wins. Hola (sweep all 90 pts) = 170 bonus or opponent reset.
